blockingIssues.problem: Insufficiently scoped headline and rationale: the idea implies a generalizable risk from adding generic editorial guardrails, but the source evidence is a single controlled change in one pipeline (Experiment 005) with three runs per condition, one prompt diff, gpt-5-mini, and explicit limitations (no seed/temperature, possible backend changes, not statistically significant).
blockingIssues.correction: Reframe the title and description to constrain the claim to this experiment and explicitly document the tested setting and limitations. For example, change the headline to: "In Experiment 005 on Nueyon.Compose, adding a generic 'Preserve Editorial Intent' rule shifted emphasis and introduced unsupported claims." In the description and rationale, add a short methods sentence naming the tested scope (Nueyon.Compose Narrative.user.prompt.txt change only; candidate vs baseline; OpenAI gpt-5-mini; LinkedInPost format; three runs per condition) and include the source's limitations (no seed/temperature, small sample size — three runs per condition — and possible backend/model alias drift). Remove or qualify any wording that implies a universal or statistically established effect (e.g., replace broad statements like "can backfire" presented as general guidance with "did backfire in this experiment" or "may pose a risk in similar settings; further testing required"). Also recommend that downstream guidance advise replicating the change (A/B or targeted runs using the rubric and hard gates) before promotion. This correction preserves the experiment's observed result while making its scope and uncertainty explicit, addressing the requirement that a general takeaway identify the particular trial and tested setting.
